breadcrumb: Environmental graphics for a connected place
h1: Environmental graphics for a connected place
lead: Environmental graphics bring branding, storytelling and useful information into the physical space. A wall, a pane of glass and a directional panel can each serve a different role while sharing a clear visual language. For New York workplaces, retail interiors and managed properties, Vision Graphics can help frame a coordinated program around the journey through the building. Start with what people should notice, understand and do at each point, then select the surfaces and graphic treatments that support those goals.

sections.h2: Create a sequence, not a collection
sections.html: Identify arrival, orientation, destination and gathering areas on a floor plan. A strong arrival graphic can introduce the identity, while quieter directional elements guide movement. Repeated colors or motifs can connect the experience, but they should not make decorative messages look like essential instructions.

sections.h2: Coordinate with the space and its teams
sections.html: Bring interior finishes, lighting plans and room names into the brief. Each surface may need a different production approach, and work may need to align with construction or tenant schedules. Review artwork, measurements and property responsibilities before breaking the program into production packages.

items.p: Use murals, timelines or values displays to express identity at room scale.
Coordinate privacy patterns and branding with adjacent interior graphics.
Connect directories, directionals and destination signs through one visual system.

items.q: What is the first planning document?
items.a_html: A floor plan with the intended visitor journey and a list of graphic locations gives the project a useful structure.
A shared design system can support phases. Confirm materials and artwork records so later additions remain consistent.
